data.name: Tirzah
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew Bible, Tirzah is a place name that appears in the Book of Joshua as one of the cities assigned to the tribe of Joseph. It is believed to be the site of an ancient spring or well, and the name may derive from the Hebrew words צרה (tsara) 'joy, delight' or תרזה (tirzah) 'my delight'. In the New Testament, Tirzah is mentioned in the Revelation of John as one of the cities of the tribes of Israel.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the joy and happiness that comes from living in harmony with God and His teachings.
data.numerology_meaning: A leader and pioneer, you are ambitious, creative, and driven.

in_hebrew.name: תירצה
in_hebrew.meaning: תירצה - שמה של בתו של צלאפד במשפחת מנשה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: תירצה היא שם של בתו של צלאפד, בן משפחת מנשה. השם תירצה מוזכר בספר במדבר, פרק כ״ז, פסוקים כ״ד-ל״א, ופרק לו, פסוקים י״א-י״ג. לפי המסורת היהודית, תירצה הייתה אחת מחמש בנותיו של צלאפד, שדרשו את נחלתן מאת משה רבינו. השם תירצה נגזר מהמילה הארמית 'תרצה', שפירושה 'רצויה' או 'אהובה'.

in_greek.name: Τιρζα
in_greek.meaning: Τιρζα - κόρη του Σελαφάδ εν τη φυλή Μανασσή
in_greek.long_meaning: Τιρζα (Tirza) αναφέρεται στην κόρη του Σελαφάδ, μέλους της φυλής Μανασσή. Το όνομα Τιρζα εμφανίζεται στο Βιβλίο των Αριθμών, κεφάλαιο 27, εδάφια 24-31, και κεφάλαιο 36, εδάφια 11-13. Σύμφωνα με την εβραϊκή παράδοση, η Τιρζα ήταν μία από τις πέντε κόρες του Σελαφάδ, οι οποίες ζήτησαν από τον Μωυσή τη διανομή της κληρονομιάς τους. Το όνομα Τιρζα πιθανόν να προέρχεται από την αρامی λέξη 'תרצה' (Teretzah), που σημαίνει 'επιθυμητή' ή 'αγαπημένη'.

in_latin.name: Tirza
in_latin.meaning: Tirza - filia Selaphad in tribu Manasse
in_latin.long_meaning: Tirza est nomen filiae Selaphad, qui fuit de tribu Manasse. Nomen Tirza invenitur in libro Numerorum, capitulo 27, versibus 24-31, et capitulo 36, versibus 11-13. Iuxta traditionem Iudaicam, Tirza fuit una ex quinque filiabus Selaphad, quae a Moyse hereditatem suam postulaverunt. Nomen Tirza derivatum est ex voce aramaica 'תרצה' (Teretzah), quae significat 'desiderata' vel 'amata'.

in_english.name: Tirzah
in_english.meaning: Daughter of Selaphad, desired one, beloved
in_english.long_meaning: Tirzah is a biblical name originating from the Hebrew 'Tirzah' (תירצה), meaning 'she who is desired' or 'beloved'. It is mentioned in the book of Numbers, 27:24-31 and 36:11-13, as the name of one of the five daughters of Selaphad, a member of the tribe of Manasseh. According to Jewish tradition, these daughters requested their inheritance from Moses. The name Tirzah symbolizes a cherished and loved individual. Throughout Christian tradition, Tirzah is recognized as a significant biblical name reflecting the cultural and spiritual heritage of the early Christian community.

biblical_reference.note: One of the five daughters of Selaphad

data.cultural_impact: The name Tirzah holds cultural significance as a place name in the Hebrew Bible and New Testament. It suggests a rich and storied history, linking individuals to the biblical past and the heritage of the Israelites. The name's connection to the city of Tirzah and its association with springs or wells adds a layer of symbolism, perhaps evoking images of fertility, renewal, and nourishment.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Tirzah holds spiritual significance in its potential association with joy, delight, and my delight. The biblical origins of the name suggest a connection to the inner workings of one's soul, offering a reminder to focus on finding happiness and delight in life, as well as in one's heartfelt relationship with God. The name may serve as a reminder of the spiritual nourishment available through faith and the importance of cultivating a deep, joyful connection with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Tirzah is mentioned in the Old Testament as one of the daughters of Jacob and one of the cities in the territory of the tribe of Zebulun (Joshua 19:13). The name Tirzah is most likely derived from Hebrew words meaning 'pleasant' or 'delightful'.

historical_references.reference: During the reign of King Jeroboam II of the Northern Kingdom of Israel (783-742 BCE), Tirzah is recorded as a major city in the region. It is mentioned in the Bible as one of the capitals of the Northern Kingdom along with Samaria.
